newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures crumble on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures crumble on profit-taking.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures fell back sharply on Monday as dealers took profits after several weeks of upward moves.
"I think it is profit-taking after two to three weeks of going up," said one local futures dealer. "I think it will be down again tomorrow and probably on Wednesday before it comes back for a rally."
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract settled at 18,865 points, down 230 on volume of 18,135 lots.

The March contract opened firmer on continued bullish sentiment over the prospects for a recovery of the Japanese economy, but dealers said gains were eroded after buy backs of bank and construction shares faltered.

"The movement is still generally higher but I think it will take a while to achieve our target of 20,000 points," said a dealer. "Eventually we will get to 20,000, but not in the next two weeks....It may be two or three months."
Dealers said the March contract was now within a wide, 1,000-point trading band between 18,500 and 19,500.
